blocks.content: The Constitution is not a mere lawyers' document, it is a vehicle of Life, and its spirit is always the spirit of Age.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Constitution of India was adopted by the Constituent Assembly on November 26, 1949, and came into force on January 26, 1950.
Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies) was described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar as the 'Heart and Soul' of the Indian Constitution.
The 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1976 added the terms 'Socialist', 'Secular', and 'Integrity' to the Preamble.
Part III (Articles 12 to 35) guarantees Fundamental Rights, which are enforceable by law through judicial review.
The Directive Principles of State Policy (DPSP) in Part IV are non-justiciable guidelines meant for socio-economic welfare.

rows: Borrowed from US Constitution (Bill of Rights)

items: High Probability: Frequently tested amendments include the 42nd (Mini-Constitution), 44th (Right to Property made legal right), and 86th (Right to Education).
Article 368 under Part XX details the procedure for amending the Constitution, requiring specific majorities.
Be clear on the distinction between Fundamental Rights (enforceable in court) and DPSP (non-enforceable guidance for governance).
